scope: Ten selected originals read only at specified pages. No exhaustive novelty, priority, original proof completeness, or independent replication claim.

papers.title: Quantum machine learning in feature Hilbert spaces
papers.finding: Quantum feature spaces, inner products and squared-overlap kernels already established; no novelty for that identity.
papers.limit: Scope reading only; no claim that the trainable normalized Q-RMEA family is equivalent to an unconstrained SVM.

papers.title: Supervised quantum machine learning models are kernel methods
papers.finding: Density-matrix feature maps with Hilbert-Schmidt inner products directly cover the basic Tr(E rho) representation.
papers.limit: No whole-family equivalence asserted when preparation is learned or constrained.

papers.title: Quantum Self-Attention Neural Networks for Text Classification
papers.authors: Guangxi Li; Xuanqiang Zhao; Xin Wang
papers.finding: Gaussian projected quantum attention, normalized classical aggregation, and explicit discussion of direct squared-overlap attention on p4. Different from global relation-hypothesis effects over frozen RoBERTa features.
papers.limit: No first-of-kind quantum attention claim; original p4 rendered and visually checked; their qualitative limitation is not accepted as an impossibility theorem.

papers.title: Quantum steering
papers.authors: Roope Uola; Ana C. S. Costa; H. Chau Nguyen; Otfried Guhne
papers.finding: Steering requires an assemblage incompatible with a local hidden-state model; normalized conditional token weights alone do not demonstrate EPR steering.
papers.limit: Review provides terminology; no new steerability criterion transferred or certified.

papers.title: The Dawn of Quantum Natural Language Processing
papers.authors: Riccardo Di Sipio; Jia-Hong Huang; Samuel Yen-Chi Chen; Stefano Mangini; Marcel Worring
papers.finding: VQC query/key/value transforms and ordinary softmax attention predate current method; different output pooling architecture.
papers.limit: This original p4 does not itself establish the exact Born-overlap implementation described by the later QSANN paper.

papers.title: When Normalization Selects the Sign: Auditing Robustness Ablations in Quantum Attention
papers.authors: Owen Friedewald; Srikar Alla; Ali Shiri Sichani; Chi-Ren Shyu
papers.finding: Normalization and comparison definition can change ablation interpretation; elementary formulas explicitly used as design checks rather than novel general theory.
papers.limit: Different generated physical robustness task; no performance or attribution conclusion imported to Re-TACRED.

papers.title: Higher-Order Token Interactions via Quantum Attention
papers.authors: Jian Xu; Chao Li; Delu Zeng; John Paisley; Qibin Zhao
papers.finding: Joint-token quantum interaction circuit differs from per-token Q-RMEA preparation. Their p5 generic low-degree explanation needs correction: an exact three-token softmax cubic counterexample exists.
papers.limit: Counterexample refutes that generic Fourier inference, not their full fixed-precision asymptotic MATCHk bound. No automatic high-order claim for Q-RMEA.

papers.title: Reversing quantum dynamics with near-optimal quantum and classical fidelity
papers.finding: Section V Eq37 defines the known square-root/pretty-good measurement. Q-RMEA token-frame whitening gives exactly this measurement for a regularized uniform token ensemble.
papers.limit: State-discrimination average fidelity guarantees do not automatically imply downstream semantic attention or classifier utility for an arbitrary learned query.

papers.title: Attention is not Explanation
papers.finding: Counterfactual attention includes repeated random permutations with frozen hidden representations and explicit output-distribution distances. Direct prior for interpreting weight interventions; no automatic novelty for permutation sensitivity.
papers.limit: No exhaustive claim about CE/Bregman literature. Scope reading only.

papers.title: Attention is not not Explanation
papers.finding: Distinguishes explanations from unique explanations, discusses capacity and seed variance, and compares trained uniform attention with learned attention. Generic attention utility/faithfulness is already a crowded problem.
papers.limit: No exhaustive claim about CE/Bregman literature. Scope reading only.
